author: bereshit-rabbah

lemma.he: בֵּין מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים לְמַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים
lemma.en: between the deeds of the righteous and the deeds of the wicked

original.text: א"ר ינאי מתחלת ברייתו של עולם צפה הקב"ה מעשיהן של צדיקים ומעשיהם של רשעים. "וְהָאָרֶץ הָיְתָה תֹהוּ" אלו מעשיהם של רשעים "וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יְהִי אוֹר" אלו מעשיהן של צדיקים "וַיַּבְדֵּל אֱלֹהִים בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ" בין מעשיהן של צדיקים למעשיהן של רשעים. "וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם" אלו מעשיהן של צדיקים "וְלַחֹשֶׁךְ קָרָא לַיְלָה" אלו מעשיהן של רשעים
original.version: Sefaria 'Wikisource Bereshit Rabbah' (CC BY-SA). Phase 6, 2026-09-05: moved off 'Midrash Rabbah -- TE', whose own site asserts all rights reserved

english.text: Rabbi Yanai said: Right from the beginning of the creation of the world, the Holy One blessed be He foresaw the actions of the righteous and the actions of the wicked. “The earth was emptiness” (Genesis 1:2) – these are the actions of the wicked. “God said: Let there be light” (Genesis 1:3) – these are the actions of the righteous. “God distinguished between the light and the darkness” (Genesis 1:4) – between the actions of the righteous and the actions of the wicked. “God called the light, Day” (Genesis 1:5) – these are the actions of the righteous. “And to the darkness He called Night” (Genesis 1:5) – these are the actions of the wicked.

notes: R. Yanai runs the moral reading through the verses one clause at a time, so that nothing in Gen 1:2–5 is about light and darkness at all. The earth was tohu — the deeds of the wicked. Let there be light — the deeds of the righteous. And God divided between the light and the darkness — between the deeds of the righteous and the deeds of the wicked. He called the light day — the deeds of the righteous; and to the darkness he called night — the deeds of the wicked. It is the same reading as R. Abahu's at 2:5 with the argument taken out and the verse-by-verse mapping put in its place, and it is what Isidore, Rabanus, Remigius and the Glossa do in Latin with the same clauses, four hundred years later and to the same effect. **Slice note**: K10 built the continuation of this section as `br-3-8`, beginning at 'it was evening'; this is the part before it.
